summary: Join our GIS for Environmental Management course and master the tools to analyze spatial data. Equip yourself for effective environmental decision-making.
lede: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for Environmental Management connects spatial analysis with practical planning, helping you turn field observations, satellite imagery, permit data, and asset records into defensible environmental decisions. Using ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, ISO 14001, ISO 19115 metadata principles, and OGC interoperability practices, you will build stronger evidence about impacts, exposure, and mitigation performance. Through guided exercises, you will practise geodatabase design, coordinate reference system selection, data quality control, risk mapping, raster interpretation, overlay and buffer analysis, suitability modelling, and map-based reporting. You will finish with reusable maps, an environmental risk register, a metadata template, a monitoring design, and a practical GIS action plan, alongside introductory coverage of remote sensing, AI-assisted classification, and workflow automation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with environmental information and need to apply GIS for environmental management to real assessments, monitoring programmes, project approvals, and sustainability reporting. It suits professionals with basic mapping or data-handling experience who want structured analysis using ArcGIS Pro or QGIS.
prerequisites: You should have basic experience reading maps, handling environmental data, or supporting environmental assessments. No programming is required for completion, and the exercises use guided interfaces in QGIS and ArcGIS Pro rather than Python development. Advanced remote sensing and AI-assisted classification receive conceptual awareness and operational application coverage, not technical engineering or production deployment.
